references.text: God's mountain (Horeb) is mentioned here as the place where Moses met God in the burning bush, the same place where Aaron now meets Moses.
The Lord had previously told Moses that Aaron was on his way to meet him and that he would rejoice when he saw him.
A similar meeting and kiss is described when Moses meets his father-in-law Jethro in the wilderness.
The kiss as a greeting between relatives is a common custom, as when Laban kissed Jacob.
Esau ran toward Jacob, embraced him, and kissed him—a similar reunion between brothers.
Joseph kissed all his brothers when they were reunited in Egypt, another example of brotherly reconciliation with a kiss.
God promised Moses that the people would serve Him on this mountain after their deliverance from Egypt.
A clear narrative contrast between the beginning of the mission (the meeting at the mountain) and its conclusion (the view from the mountain).
